extracted.intended_audience: marketing and PR practitioners, small business communicators, and learners new to public relations
extracted.subtask_description: Foundational guidance for writing news-first press releases, pitching reporters, distributing PR, measuring coverage, and managing crisis communications. Covers standard press-release components, quality checks, pitching format, distribution strategy, measurement metrics, and crisis protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR as reputation management (not advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: PR is reputation management, not advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize earned coverage, long-term relationships, and substance over spin. Treat PR as part of marketing, not above it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned coverage over paid placements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize building relationships and getting editorial pickup rather than relying solely on paid placements; earned coverage carries credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term relationships over one-time wins
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in ongoing relationships with journalists and outlets instead of chasing single hit stories; value sustained trust and repeat coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over spin
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on newsworthy, factual substance rather than superficial promotion or hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR fits inside marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: PR fits inside marketing, not above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate PR strategy with broader marketing goals and metrics; align messaging and measurement with business objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: news-first, 80 chars
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a headline that leads with the news and keeps to ~80 characters. Test headline for clarity and newsworthiness (see 'would I tweet this?' test).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadline (optional)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a subheadline when you need to add context or a secondary point, but it's optional—don't force one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline: city and date
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the city and the date at the top of the release to indicate origin and timing of the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: 5 W's in 50 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the who, what, when, where, why in a concise lede of about 50 words to answer reporters' immediate questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: 3-4 paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the story in a short body of 3–4 paragraphs that expands on the lede, includes key details, and flows logically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: 25-35 words from C-level
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include one human-sounding quote of about 25–35 words from a C-level executive that adds perspective or color; ensure it sounds authentic and not scripted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: ~75 words about company
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise company boilerplate (~75 words) describing what the company does and any essential background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact info: named with phone number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a specific contact person and a phone number so reporters can easily follow up; avoid generic email-only contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: "###" end marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conventional '###' to denote the end of the press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: News passes 'outside-the-org' test
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the story would matter to people outside your organization—if not, it's likely not newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline tested with 'would I tweet this?'
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline tested with "would I tweet this?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tweet-test to judge immediacy and shareability: if the headline is something you'd share on social, it's likely crisp and news-first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote should sound human
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid corporate-speak; quotes should add human perspective and be realistic for the speaker to have said.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach multimedia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include images, video, or other assets to increase pickup likelihood and make the story more usable for outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewed by outside reader
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have someone unfamiliar with the story read the release to ensure clarity and that the news resonates externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style throughout
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AP style conventions to match journalistic standards and reduce editing friction for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized email over mass blast
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize tailored, personalized outreach to individual reporters rather than sending mass, generic blasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch subject line: news in 8 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a concise subject line that communicates the news in about eight words to capture a reporter's attention quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch body length: 100-200 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the pitch email short (100–200 words), focusing on the essential news and relevance to the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single clear ask in pitch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make one clear request in the pitch (e.g., interview, feature, link) so the reporter knows the desired next step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide phone number in pitch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a phone number in the pitch to facilitate quick follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be available for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the contact is responsive and available to provide additional information or interviews when reporters respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire services for SEO, not pickup
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire distribution primarily to aid SEO and archival presence; don't rely on wires to generate meaningful editorial pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct outreach for actual coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted outreach to specific reporters and outlets to earn real editorial coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media for amplification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage social channels to amplify coverage once earned; social helps reach audiences and can attract additional pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom for archive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a newsroom page on your site to host releases and make them discoverable and archivally accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletter inclusion when relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place important news in company newsletters when it aligns with audience interests; use newsletters selectively for amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure coverage tier and sentiment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorize coverage by outlet tier and assess sentiment (positive/neutral/negative) rather than counting raw clips alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup velocity (24-hour, 7-day)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track how quickly coverage appears after distribution—key windows include the first 24 hours and the first 7 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand mention tracking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor brand mentions across media to measure reach, context, and potential impacts on awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipeline impact (30-day)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess short-term business impact such as leads or pipeline influenced by coverage within a ~30-day window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-tail SEO (90-day)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure long-tail SEO benefits of coverage over a longer horizon (e.g., 90 days) to capture sustained organic traffic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge crisis within 2 hours
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a crisis, publicly acknowledge the issue promptly (target within two hours) to shape the narrative and reduce speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific facts, not vague statements, in crisis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, verifiable information rather than vague assurances; specificity builds credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named spokesperson with authority
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a named spokesperson who has the authority and knowledge to speak on the issue to avoid mixed messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate concrete corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specific steps the organization is taking to address the problem; avoid generic promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify update cadence during crisis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell stakeholders when they can expect the next update (e.g., hourly, daily) to manage expectations and maintain control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric — Newsworthy substance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces that the core of PR materials must be genuinely newsworthy; ties back to outside-the-org test and lede requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric — Standard format components
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates that releases should include the standard components (headline, lede, quote, boilerplate, contacts, end marker) to meet journalist expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric — Personalized distribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes targeted, personalized outreach over mass distribution to improve chances of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric — Measurement beyond impressions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates measuring outcomes (sentiment, tier, pipeline, SEO) rather than focusing only on raw impressions or clip counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric — Crisis protocol if needed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a crisis communication plan is in place and includes the listed timing, spokesperson, facts, and update cadence requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric — Long-term reputation focus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate PR success on its ability to build and protect reputation over time rather than short-term publicity spikes.
